title: config.json, a personal brain's configuration
description: The contract between the brain engine and a personal brain, the private repo of a person or a team: who decides for it, where its registry, rules, memory and records are, the engine it pins, what must never reach a public repo and the secrets it names. Read by brain config, checked by brain config --check and brain check --all. Paths are relative to the file's folder. No secret value ever: a secret is named by its environment variable only.

v.description: The contract's version: the engine refuses a version it does not know (brain config --check).

owner.description: The person or team who decides for this brain, as the views name them; the same name as owner in its graph stores' schema.yaml.

display_name.description: The name the views show for the owner (the queue's title, the help texts, the confirmations), e.g. Ada or Ada L.; default owner. owner stays the id --by writes and the stores declare: a record never changes for display.

kind.description: A person's brain or a team's; default person.

tenant.description: The tenant id when the brain is hosted for a team (HMaaS): its ledgers and keys are kept apart under that id. None for a person's own brain.

require_signed.description: The owner's opt-in to the merge lock on signed answers (brain identity, docs/identity.md): true, brain check fails on an answer of the owner-decides class (money, keys, accounts, visibility, heirs, scheduled tasks) recorded without a signature by a decider's key of members.yaml, on a signature that does not verify, and on an invalid members.yaml; default false: the same findings are warnings. Without members.yaml nothing is checked either way.

registry.description: The projects registry (brain projects, brain --project NAME); default projects.yaml.

rules.description: The owner's rules for every project, in order, as the Claude rendering injects them at the start of each session and subagent (files brain render --target claude writes from the neutral source). Default: none.

source.description: The neutral source's folder (rules with scope and id, procedures, MCP servers, packs) that brain render turns into each agent's files; default source.

memory.description: The memory notes' folder (brain memory); default memory.

records.description: The records' folder, DDR, SR and AR (brain record); default records.

template.description: The template brain init wrote this brain from (brain init --template): a later version of it is shown and applied by a plan, never over what the owner changed.

version.description: The template's version brain init rendered.

engine.description: The engine this brain runs: its repo and the tag pinned. The installer installs the brain command at that tag (pip, from the repo's packages/brain), research-graph at the same one; moved by a reviewed PR, then the installer on each machine.

repo.description: owner/name of the engine's repo on GitHub.

pin.description: The tag installed, vX.Y.Z; moved by a reviewed PR.

installer.description: This brain's own installer, relative to its root (install.ps1, say): run without arguments it prints its plan, with -Apply it installs the engine at the pin. When the installed engine lags the pin, the cockpit's u opens its plan and runs -Apply on the owner's yes; a brain without one is updated by brain update.

verify_tags.description: The owner's opt-in (wi-brain-release-signing, off by default): brain update and the engine's installer refuse a release tag that is not signed by a key of allowed_signers, the file brain identity allowed-signers --write generates beside config.json from members.yaml's releaser role. Without it they report the verification and install anyway.

adapters.description: The renderings of the brain for each agent tool. Only claude so far; wi-brain-neutral-source adds the rendering's choice.

claude.description: The names of the Claude Code rendering, read by install.ps1, the rules' linter and the guards' messages; the engine's defaults when absent (marketplace brain, plugin brain-core).

plugin.description: The core plugin: its hooks inject the rules, its guards sign their refusals with its name.

source.description: owner/name of the GitHub repo Claude Code clones the marketplace from.

sources.description: The third-party plugin sources the owner allows a session to install from (the third-party guard, wi-brain-guard-third-party): a marketplace name, which claude plugin install NAME@MARKETPLACE may name, or, with a slash or a backslash, a source claude plugin marketplace add may name (owner/repo, a git URL, a folder from the brain's root). The brain's own marketplace, source and folder always pass.

public.description: What must never reach a public repo: read by brain boundary (readiness of the engine side) and brain check --public. It stays in the private brain: copying it to a public repo would publish it.

repos.description: The public repos this brain pushes to, owner/name.

deny.description: Terms matched as whole words, case-insensitive, / and \ alike.

users.description: User names of machines and accounts.

allow.description: {glob: reason of 15 characters or more}: files where a denied term is expected, a licence's author say; brain check --public excepts them from every check but secrets.

patterns.description: {name: regular expression}: what no line of a public repo may match, a domain's own (a data venue's derived columns); brain check --public, from the domain's template.

refuse.description: {glob: reason of 15 characters or more}: files a public repo must not hold, a domain's own (the research-IP paths of a split); brain check --public.

secrets.description: {ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE: what it is for}: the secrets this brain's projects use, by name only; their values stay in each host's keystore, set by the owner.

tier.description: The profile of a machine that has no $BRAIN_HOME/profile.json of its own (brain profile set writes one): the base and the overrides every machine of this brain starts from (brain.tiers, brain doctor). Recommended is computed per machine, so it is never a default here.

base.description: lite (the core, no dependency) or default (Lite plus the extras without any service); default when absent.

components.description: {capability or stack: true|false}: the overrides (Personnalisable) over the base; brain check --all refuses an unknown name.

inventory.description: The machine inventory brain doctor (brain profile) reports.

schema.description: The inventory contract's id the report carries (schema), the owner's machines brick's format; default brain.status/v1.

probes.description: {name: probe}: the dependency probes (brain.depprobes, brain probes): each external dependency of a capability checked at zero token by the alerts pass on the machines it names, an alert probe:<name> when it is not OK. brain probes --kinds lists each kind's keys; brain config --check checks them.

kind.description: file-age (path, max_age), json-age (path, field, max_age, where), command (argv, ok_exit, expect), http (url, ok_status).

about.description: The capability that relies on it, shown in its alert.

timeout.description: How long it may take (90s, 2m); default 10s, at most 120s.

machines.description: The hosts it runs on (case-insensitive); none: every machine.

path.description: file-age, json-age: a file or a glob (the newest match); ~, the environment's variables and $BRAIN_HOME are expanded.

max_age.description: file-age, json-age: the oldest the file or the field may be (26h, 7d).

field.description: json-age: the timestamp's key, dotted for a nested one: an ISO time or seconds since the epoch.

where.description: json-age: {field: value} a JSON Lines line (the last that matches) or the JSON file must match.

argv.description: command: the program and its arguments, never through a shell (a shell or an interpreter is refused); its output is never shown.

ok_exit.description: command: the exit codes that mean OK; default [0].

expect.description: command: a regular expression its output must match.

url.description: http: the URL a GET is sent to, with no header and no user or password; never shown.

ok_status.description: http: the statuses that mean OK; default any 2xx or 3xx.

power.description: The owner's platform as the power guard knows it by name (brain.guards): what acts on a node beyond the engine's own list (shutdown, reboot, Wake-on-LAN, k3s, kubectl writes).

node_clis.description: The node lifecycle CLIs: every verb but their reads acts on a node; one named kubectl-<name> is a kubectl plugin, kubectl <name> too. guard.sh's pre-filter reads them from <BRAIN_HOME>/cache/node-clis.txt, which the guard keeps current.

node_services.description: The node agents' services: stopping one acts on a node.

branches.description: The branch names the branches guard lets a session create in the registry's repos (brain.guards): git checkout -b, git switch -c, git worktree add -b, git branch NAME, gh pr create's head; main and master always pass.

allowed.description: Each entry a prefix ending in / (feat/: feat/<slug>) or a pattern whose <slug> (lowercase letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'), <host> and <date> (YYYY-MM-DD) stand for one part; default the engine's list (brain.guards.BRANCHES).

brief.description: brain brief's parameters (wi-brain-brief-generate): each task class's model, effort and default context budget, and the headings of the owner's rules it copies (the definition of done, the never-list), and its after-the-merge lines.

classes.description: {class: {model, effort, budget}}: the model and effort the coordinator starts a session of that class with (an empty string: the coordinator's own), and its default budget (400k, 600k, 800k or 1M); default the engine's (brain.brief.CLASSES: trivial a small model at low effort, strategic the strongest at high effort).

done.description: The heading of the rules' section copied as the definition of done (default 'Definition of done').

never.description: The heading of the rules' section copied as the never-list (default 'Never'); without one, the rules' sentences that start with Never and their '<owner> decides' lines.

after_merge.description: The lines of the brief's 'After the merge' section (default the engine's, brain.brief.AFTER_MERGE: the session that merges its own PR archives itself after its after-merge steps, the coordinator archives a child reported merged and verified without asking again, never another running session or one with uncommitted or unmerged work, and the owner's auto_archive_inactive_days net); [] drops the section.

usage.description: The token ledger's parameters (brain usage, brain cost): the plan in force from a day on (a label: costs are API prices whatever the plan), and prices that replace or add to the built-in list.

plans.description: The plan in force from each since day (YYYY-MM-DD; an empty string for the start).

monthly.description: its monthly price, once the owner gives it

prices.description: {model id: [input, output, cache read, cache write 5 min, cache write 1 h]} in USD per million tokens.

master_budget.description: A master session's context budget in tokens when its brief gives none (brain sessions, the cockpit's Ctx %, the master's watch in brain.budget): default the model's window, 1000000.

guard.description: The usage governor's thresholds and caps (brain.governor, the PreToolUse hook on start_session, Agent and Workflow; brain usage guard shows them): ask the owner at warn, refuse at critical, past a cap or while the newest quota reading is stale. A project of the registry may lower sessions and brainstorms for itself (usage: in projects.yaml), never raise them.

enabled.description: false turns the governor off (default true)

warn.description: % of a quota window used from which a new session, subagent or workflow asks the owner (default 80)

critical.description: % of a quota window used from which they are refused (default 95)

sessions.description: the sessions running in parallel on this machine, at most (default 8); lowered to what the week's room pays for

brainstorms.description: the brainstorms open at once on this machine, every project counted (default 2)

memory.description: % of committed memory (Windows: RAM plus page file promised, of the commit limit; elsewhere the memory in use) from which a new session or workflow is refused (default 97)

memory_available_gb.description: GB of available RAM under which a new session or workflow is refused (default 0: no floor; the owner opts in, e.g. 4)

wave_hours.description: the hours a wave is planned for, in the quota cap (default 4)

session_hour_usd.description: the API-price cost of one session-hour, in the quota cap (default 14)

session_hour_measured.description: true: the quota cap uses the measured session-hour (brain usage quota's, its agents included) when it is above session_hour_usd; false (default): the configured session_hour_usd only, the measured value shown

fresh_minutes.description: a new session or workflow is refused while the newest quota reading is older (default 60; 0: never)

live_minutes.description: a session counts as running when active this recently (default 30)

brainstorm_hours.description: a brainstorm counts as open when active this recently and not archived (default 12)

brainstorm_title.description: the regular expression a brainstorm's title matches, besides its brief's Task class: brainstorm or #brainstorm (default ^\W*brainstorm\b, case ignored)

scopes.description: The scope tree's file (spec-brain-scope-tree 3.13), relative to this file; default scopes.yaml beside it when there is one ($BRAIN_SCOPES names another). brain classes reads its class floors, brain vault the recipients its nodes add.

classes.description: The data class of every store and where it may go (brain classes, brain check --all refuse a store without a class and a destination its class forbids). docs/data-classes.md; the matrix: brain classes --matrix.

stores.description: {store: {class, paths, to, waive, project, why}}, in order: the first store whose glob matches a tracked file classes it (specific stores first, a catch-all ** last). The engine's machine stores ($BRAIN_HOME/ledger, sessions, resume, digest, vault, ~/.claude/projects) must be declared too.

class.description: public, private, confidential, sealed, resident, secret, or tenant:<id> for a hosted team's store.

paths.description: Globs over the repo's tracked files (** any folders, * within a name), or machine paths: $BRAIN_HOME/... or ~/...

to.description: The exits the store takes; one its class says never for is refused, an opt-in one needs naming here.

waive.description: {exit: reason of 15 characters or more}: a refusal of its class kept as a known, printed gap (the confidential stores in clear in the private remote until the encrypted-git trial decides).

project.description: The registry's project the store belongs to, for its scope floor and its recipients along the scope chain; default the brain's own project.

feature_coverage_strict.description: The owner's opt-in to fix the feature coverage of what a change touches: true, brain audit --diff makes a touched command or module of a command registry that no feature names a LEFT line (to fix in the PR, within --limit); default false: a DEFER line to the repo's debt item. An added one is a NEW line either way, on a unit feature.links already makes NEW (no implemented_by of its file).

norm_lints_strict.description: The owner's opt-in to the norm lints (brain.norms): true, brain audit --diff makes each norm a change adds to a touched Python file (a subprocess or urlopen without a timeout, a text open() or read_text/write_text without an encoding, a naive datetime stored, a secret in a child's argv or env) a NEW line, to fix in the PR or justify; default false: an info line, never blocking. Those already in a touched file are DEFER lines to the repo's debt item either way.

features.description: The feature matrix's opt-ins (brain features, README, The feature matrix of each repo).

public_strict.description: The owner's opt-in to hold a public clone's FEATURES.md to the public render: true, brain audit (check features.md) and brain features render without --write refuse the full render in a checkout whose remote is in public.repos; default false: the full render passes too (brain check --public still reads it). The public render is what --write writes either way.

views.description: The generated views and their one writer (brain views, docs/views.md).

strict.description: The owner's opt-in to the one writer's rules: true, brain check and brain refresh fail (exit 1) on a stale view on the default branch, and brain audit --write, coverage --write, features render --write, decision view --write and modules --write refuse an engine other than engine.pin (unless --force); default false: a stale view on the default branch is a warning, and those writers write with any engine. brain views --write holds its own output to the strict rules either way.

hints.description: The opt-in hooks that hint, never refuse: brain render --target claude (brain sync) registers each only when it is true.

read.description: The read hint (readhint.sh, brain.readhint, PreToolUse on Read, Grep, Bash and PowerShell, about 0.2 s per call): true, brain render --target claude (brain sync) registers it in the core plugin's hooks.json; default false: not registered, no call pays its cost. BRAIN_READ_HINT=0 turns it off in a session while it is on.

vault.description: brain vault: the public keys stores are sealed to, never a private key (brain vault recipient add and brain check --all refuse one). docs/runbooks/vault.md.

adapter.description: The adapter preferred; default age when found and every recipient has an age key, else gpg.

min_recipients.description: The recipients every sealed store needs, two at least (a device key and the recovery key); default 2.

canary_hours.description: How old a canary may be before brain health vault fails; default 26 (a daily run and some slack).

recipients.description: {name: {kind, age, gpg, host, classes, why}}: the public recipients. A recipient named by a scope node (scopes.yaml vault.recipients) or a tenant is added only for those stores; the others are the root's, for every store.

kind.description: device (one per machine, in its OS keystore), recovery (offline, on paper), hardware (a YubiKey), person (a member's key).

age.description: An age recipient (age1..., or an ssh-ed25519 / ssh-rsa public key).

gpg.description: An armored gpg public key file, relative to this file (vault/keys/<name>.asc).

host.description: The machine a device key belongs to.

classes.description: The classes this recipient may read (an instance on a placement that allows only some); default every class.

tenants.description: {tenant id: [recipient names]}: a tenant:<id> store is sealed to its tenant's recipients only (the tenant keeps its keys).

spool.description: brain spool: the sealed local spool of the stores that leave the machine, pushed by hand (brain spool push). Optional: without it the spool holds ledger, usage and sessions and keeps its files on this machine. docs/vault.md.

stores.description: The stores brain spool push seals into the spool, declared in classes.stores; default ledger, usage and sessions.

remote.description: A folder the sealed files are sent to, each copy checked by sha256 (a mounted share, a synced drive; ~ and environment variables expanded); default none: they wait in $BRAIN_HOME/spool.

keep.description: The snapshots kept per store in the spool, the newest; default 3. A file put with its own paths (the session archive) is pruned only once sent, past the newest 3 of them.

max_age_days.description: How old the last push without an error may be before brain health spool warns; default 7.
